question: A triangle has two sides of length $6$ cm and $9$ cm. The third side is $x$ cm, where $x$ is a whole number. How many different values can $x$ have?

title: Apply Theorem 15: Converse of Pythagoras
question: A triangle has sides of length $20$ cm, $99$ cm and $101$ cm. Show that the triangle is right-angled.

title: Apply Corollary 4: A right angle at the circle stands on a diameter

title: Apply Theorem 17: A diagonal bisects the area of a parallelogram
question: The area of the parallelogram $PQRS$ is $420$ m$^2$. (i) Find the area of the triangle $PQR$. (ii) $T$ is the midpoint of $[QR]$. Find the area of the triangle $PQT$.

title: Apply Theorem 18: Area of a parallelogram = base × height

title: Apply Theorem 16: Base × height is the same for every side of a triangle
question:
$PQRS$ is a parallelogram with area $360\ \text{m}^2$. $T$ is the midpoint of $[QR]$.
(i) Find the area of the triangle $PQS$.
(ii) Find the area of the triangle $PQT$.

title: Apply Theorem 20: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact (and converse)

A circle has centre $O$ and radius $5$ cm. $[PT]$ is a tangent to the circle at $T$, and $|OP| = 13$ cm.
(i) Find $|PT|$.
(ii) Find the area of the triangle $OTP$.

title: Apply Corollary 1: A diagonal divides a parallelogram into two congruent triangles
question: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. $|\angle ABC| = (4x + 10)^\circ$ and $|\angle CDA| = (6x - 20)^\circ$. Find $x$ and $|\angle ABC|$.

title: Apply Theorem 13: Similar triangles have proportional sides

title: Apply Theorem 21: Perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord; perpendicular bisector of a chord passes through the centre

title: Apply Theorem 12: A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two in the same ratio

question: Construct the parallelogram $ABCD$ with $|AB| = 6$ cm, $|AD| = 4$ cm and $|\angle DAB| = 70^\circ$.

title: Construction 16: Circumcentre and circumcircle of a triangle (straight edge and compass)
question: Construct the circumcentre and circumcircle of the triangle $ABC$ with $|AB| = 7$ cm, $|BC| = 6$ cm and $|AC| = 5$ cm. Use a compass and straight edge and show your construction lines.

title: Construction 17: Incentre and incircle of a triangle (straight edge and compass)
question: Construct the incircle of the triangle $ABC$ with $|AB| = 8$ cm, $|BC| = 7$ cm and $|AC| = 5$ cm. Show all construction lines.

title: Construction 19: Tangent to a circle at a given point on it
question: A circle has centre $O$ and radius $4$ cm. $P$ is a point on the circle. Construct the tangent to the circle at $P$.

question: The triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(1, 2)$, $B(7, 4)$ and $C(4, 9)$. Find the midpoint $D$ of $[BC]$, then find the centroid $G$ of the triangle.

question: Statement: "If $x = 3$, then $x^2 = 9$." (a) Write down the converse. (b) Is the converse true or false? Give a reason.

title: Construction 7: Divide a segment into any number of equal parts without measuring
question: Divide the segment $[AB]$ into three equal parts, using only a compass and straight edge.

title: Construction 22: Orthocentre of a triangle

question: Starting with a segment of length 1 unit, construct a segment of length $\sqrt{3}$ units. Show by calculation that its length is $\sqrt{3}$.

question: Prove that $2x + 3 = 11$ if and only if $x = 4$.

question: Solve $4^{x+2} = 32^{x-1}$ for $x$.

question: Find the value of $2\log_3 6 + \log_3 15 - \log_3 20$.

question: Prove that $\sqrt{3}$ is irrational.

title: Integrate using a trig formula

(a) Find the relative frequency of landing point up.

question:
A cafe lunch deal is one soup, one sandwich and one drink. There are 2 soups, 5 sandwiches and 3 drinks.
(a) How many different deals are there?

A fair coin is tossed and a fair spinner numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 is spun.
(a) List all the possible outcomes.

(ii) Favourite subject
(iii) Time taken to run 100 m

title: Distinguish population and sample; judge generalisation
question: A researcher asks 100 students in one Dublin school how many hours they sleep. She wants to know about all 400 000 second-level students in Ireland. Name the population and the sample. Can she use the result for all Irish students? Give a reason.

title: Find mean, median and mode (incl. frequency tables)
question:
The table shows the number of books 20 students read last month.
Books read, $x$: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
Number of students, $f$: 2, 3, 6, 4, 5
Find the mean, the median and the mode.

title: Draw bar, pie, line plot, histogram and stem-and-leaf
question:
60 students were asked how they travel to school.
Bus: 24, Car: 18, Walk: 12, Cycle: 6
Find the angle for each sector of a pie chart of this data.

title: Select a simple random sample and spot bias
question:
A school has 600 students. The principal wants to survey 30 of them about the canteen. She asks the first 30 students who arrive at school in the morning.
Give one reason this sample could be biased. Describe how to pick a simple random sample of 30 instead.

title: Identify surveys, observational studies and designed experiments
question:
A researcher wants to know if a new fertiliser makes tomato plants grow taller. She splits 40 plants at random into two equal groups. One group gets the fertiliser and the other does not. After 6 weeks she measures every plant.
What type of study is this? Give a reason.

title: Find quartiles and the interquartile range
question:
The number of text messages Aoife sent on eight days was:
$11, 4, 18, 7, 20, 13, 8, 15$
Find the interquartile range.

title: Read scatter plots and correlation
question:
A teacher records hours of TV watched, $x$, and test score, $y$, for five students.
$x$: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
$y$: 9, 7, 6, 3, 2
The points lie close to a straight line sloping downhill. Choose the value of $r$ from $0.99$, $-0.2$, $-0.99$ and explain your choice.

title: Recognise outliers
question:
Find any outliers in this data set, using the rule that an outlier lies more than $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ above $Q_3$ or below $Q_1$.
$3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 30$

title: Estimate the mean of grouped data
question:
The table shows the number of minutes 20 students spent on homework.
Minutes: 0–10, 10–20, 20–30, 30–40
Number of students: 3, 7, 6, 4
Estimate the mean time.

title: Select an appropriate graphical/numerical summary
question: Six students are asked how much pocket money they get each week (in euro): $5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 40$. Which average describes a typical student better, the mean or the median? Calculate both and give a reason.

title: Describe a distribution's shape
question: The number of text messages sent by eight students in one day is: $1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 24$. Find the mean and the median. What does this tell you about the shape of the distribution?

title: Compare data sets with back-to-back stem-and-leaf plots
question: The times, in seconds, that seven students took to finish a puzzle in two weeks are: Week 1: $28, 35, 21, 47, 33, 24, 42$. Week 2: $36, 22, 31, 18, 38, 29, 23$. Show the data on a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot and compare the two weeks using the median and the range.

title: Design a plan and questions to collect data
question: A school of $800$ students has four year groups of $200$. The principal wants to find out what students think of the canteen, and plans to ask: "Don't you agree the canteen food is awful?" She will survey $40$ students. Rewrite the question fairly and say how many students to ask from each year group.

title: Use percentiles for relative standing
question:
Twenty students sat a test. Their scores, in order, were:
$34, 41, 45, 48, 52, 55, 57, 60, 62, 64, 66, 68, 70, 71, 73, 75, 78, 82, 85, 91$
Find the $80$th percentile score.

title: Define stratified, cluster and quota sampling; role of randomisation and controls
question: A school has $900$ students: $270$ in 1st year, $225$ in 2nd, $180$ in 3rd, $135$ in 4th and $90$ in 5th. A survey needs a stratified random sample of $60$ students, by year group. Name the method and find how many 3rd years are chosen.

title: Calculate the correlation coefficient (calculator)
question:
Five students recorded hours of revision $x$ and test mark $y$:
$(1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 4), (4, 7), (5, 9)$.
Find the correlation coefficient $r$, correct to $3$ decimal places, and say what it shows.

title: Draw a line of best fit by eye and predict
question:
The table shows hours of study $x$ and test mark $y$ for eight students.
$(1, 13), (2, 17), (3, 19), (4, 25), (5, 27), (6, 31), (7, 37), (8, 39)$
A line of best fit drawn by eye passes through $(2, 16)$ and $(8, 40)$. Find its equation and use it to predict the mark for a student who studies for $6$ hours.

title: Explain the effect of outliers on summary statistics
question: Seven students recorded the minutes they spent on homework: $12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 45$. The value $45$ is removed. Find how much the mean falls and how much the median falls. Which one is affected more by the outlier, and why?

title: Analyse plots to explain differences in centre and spread
question: Two classes sat the same test. Five scores are taken from each. Class A: $10, 12, 13, 14, 16$. Class B: $8, 12, 14, 16, 20$. Find the mean and standard deviation of each class and compare the two classes.

title: Recognise how sampling variability affects conclusions
question: A school has $1200$ students. Two different samples of $50$ students are asked if they walk to school. In the first sample $20$ walk. In the second sample $26$ walk. Find the proportion that walk in each sample. Why do the two answers differ, and what can you say about all $1200$ students?

title: Calculate the margin of error for a proportion
question: A survey asks $750$ people which radio station they prefer. Find the margin of error, as a percentage correct to one decimal place.

title: Interpret a histogram in terms of distribution
question:
The histogram shows the time, in minutes, that 60 students spent on homework one night. The classes and the number of students in each are: 0–20: 5; 20–40: 22; 40–60: 8; 60–80: 4; 80–100: 21.
(i) Describe the shape of the histogram.
(ii) Estimate the mean.
(iii) What does the histogram tell you about the students?

title: Interpret an analysis and relate it to the original question
question:
A survey of 400 adults found that 54% support a new bike lane. A councillor says: "The survey proves that more than half of all adults support the bike lane."
Find the margin of error and a 95% confidence interval for the percentage of all adults who support the bike lane. Is the councillor right?

title: State null and alternative hypotheses
question:
A cinema says that 45% of its customers buy popcorn. In a random sample of 625 customers, 250 bought popcorn.
Write down $H_0$ and $H_1$. Use the margin of error to test the cinema's claim and state your conclusion.

title: Test a claim about a proportion using margin of error
question:
A company says that 45% of its customers are under 30. In a random sample of 400 customers, 164 were under 30.
State $H_0$ and $H_1$. Find the margin of error and a 95% confidence interval. Test the company's claim and state your conclusion.

title: Use the sampling distribution of the mean
question: The weight of a bag of flour is normally distributed with mean $500$ g and standard deviation $12$ g. A sample of $36$ bags is taken. Find the probability that the mean weight of the sample is greater than $503$ g.

title: Construct a 95% confidence interval for a proportion
question: In a random sample of $500$ voters, $120$ say they will vote for a new candidate. Find a $95\%$ confidence interval for the proportion of all voters who will vote for her. Give the limits to $4$ decimal places.

title: Construct a 95% confidence interval for a mean (large sample)
question: A sample of $64$ batteries has a mean life of $41.5$ hours. The standard deviation of the life of all batteries is $6$ hours. Find a $95\%$ confidence interval for the mean life of all batteries.

title: Perform a two-tailed z-test of a population mean
question: A machine is set to fill bags with a mean of $250$ g. The standard deviation is $6$ g. A sample of $36$ bags has a mean of $247.9$ g. Test, at the $5\%$ level of significance, whether the mean fill has changed. State your hypotheses and your conclusion.

title: Calculate and interpret a p-value
question: A machine is set to fill bags with a mean mass of $500$ g and a standard deviation of $12$ g. A sample of $36$ bags has a mean mass of $504.6$ g. Test, at the $5\%$ level, whether the mean mass has changed. Use a $p$-value.

title: Relate confidence level, sample size and interval width
question: In a poll, $40\%$ of the people sampled support a proposal. A $95\%$ confidence interval for the proportion who support it must have a margin of error of at most $0.03$. Find the smallest sample size, $n$, that does this.

title: Standardise a value
question: The marks in an exam are normally distributed with mean $58$ and standard deviation $12$. Find the percentage of students who scored more than $73$.

title: Make decisions with the empirical rule
question: The lifetime of a battery is normally distributed with mean $60$ hours and standard deviation $5$ hours. Use the empirical rule to find the percentage of batteries that last more than $70$ hours.

title: Read probabilities from normal tables
question: The mass of a bag of sugar is normally distributed with mean $500$ g and standard deviation $8$ g. Find the probability that a bag has mass greater than $512$ g.

title: Work backwards from a normal probability
question: The marks in an exam are normally distributed with mean $58$ and standard deviation $9$. The top $20\%$ of students get a distinction. Find the lowest mark that gets a distinction, to the nearest whole number.

title: Use radian measure
question: A sector of a circle has radius $6$ cm and angle $150^\circ$. (i) Write $150^\circ$ in radians. (ii) Find the area of the sector, in terms of $\pi$.

title: Define sin θ, cos θ, tan θ for all θ (unit circle)
question: Find the exact value of $\cos 210^\circ$.

title: Use cos²A + sin²A = 1 (formula 1)
question: Given that $\sin A = \frac{8}{17}$ and $90° < A < 180°$, find the value of $\tan A$.

title: Use trig ratios in surd form
question: Find the exact value of $\sin 135° + \cos 150°$.

title: Solve sin θ = k, cos θ = k, tan θ = k in a range
question: Solve $2\sin\theta + 1 = 0$ for $0° \le \theta \le 360°$.

title: Graph sin, cos and tan
question: Sketch the graph of $f(x) = 3\cos x + 1$ for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$. Write down its period and its range.

title: Derive formula 1: cos²A + sin²A = 1
question: The point $P$ lies on the unit circle, at angle $A$ from the positive $x$-axis. Use the right-angled triangle formed by $P$ to prove that $\cos^2 A + \sin^2 A = 1$.

title: Apply compound angle formulae (4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10)
question: Use a compound angle formula to find the exact value of $\cos 105°$. Give your answer in surd form.

title: Solve trig equations giving all solutions
question: Solve $\sin 2x = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$. Give your answers in radians, in terms of $\pi$.

title: Graph and analyse a + b sin cθ / a + b cos cθ
question: The depth of water in a harbour is modelled by $h(t) = 8 + 3\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)$ metres, where $t$ is the time in hours. Find the period and the range of $h$.

title: Derive formula 2: the sine rule
question: In triangle $ABC$ the sides opposite $A$, $B$ and $C$ are $a$, $b$ and $c$. Using area $=\tfrac12 ab\sin C$, prove that $\dfrac{a}{\sin A}=\dfrac{b}{\sin B}=\dfrac{c}{\sin C}$.

title: Solve trig equations reducible to quadratics
question: Solve $2\cos^2\theta + 3\sin\theta = 3$ for $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$.

title: Apply product-to-sum and sum-to-product formulae (17–24)
question: Show that $\dfrac{\sin 7x-\sin x}{\cos 7x+\cos x}=\tan 3x$.

title: Apply double/half angle formulae (6, 11–16)
question: $A$ is an acute angle and $\sin A=\dfrac{5}{13}$. Find the exact value of $\sin 2A$ and of $\cos 2A$.

title: Derive formula 3: the cosine rule
question: Put $C$ at the origin and $A$ at $(b, 0)$. The side $CB$ has length $a$ and makes angle $C$ with $CA$. Use the distance formula to derive the cosine rule for $c = AB$.

title: Prove a trig identity
question: Prove that $\dfrac{\sin 2A}{1 + \cos 2A} = \tan A$.

title: Derive formula 4: cos(A − B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B
question: The points $P(\cos A, \sin A)$ and $Q(\cos B, \sin B)$ lie on the unit circle with centre $O$. The angle $POQ$ is $A - B$. Find $PQ^2$ in two ways and so derive a formula for $\cos(A - B)$.

title: Derive formula 5: cos(A + B) from formula 4
question: Use the formula $\cos(A - B) = \cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B$ to derive a formula for $\cos(A + B)$.

title: Derive formula 7: sin(A + B) from formula 4
question: Using $\cos(A-B)=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B$, show that $\sin(A-B)=\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B$.

title: Derive formula 6: cos 2A = cos²A − sin²A from formula 5
question: Using $\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B$, show that $\cos 2A=2\cos^2 A-1$.

title: Derive formula 9: tan(A + B) from formulae 5 and 7
question: Using $\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B$ and $\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B$, show that $\tan 2A=\dfrac{2\tan A}{1-\tan^2 A}$.

title: Use sin, cos, tan in a right-angled triangle
question: A ladder 6 m long leans against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is 2 m from the wall. Find the angle the ladder makes with the ground. Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

title: Solve 2D problems with Pythagoras
question: A ladder $7$ m long leans against a vertical wall. Its foot is $2$ m from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach? Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

title: Solve heights-and-distances problems
question: A tree stands on level ground. From a point $45$ m from its base, the angle of elevation of the top of the tree is $28°$. Find the height of the tree, correct to one decimal place.

title: Find the area of a triangle with ½ab sin C
question: In triangle $ABC$, $|AB| = 9$ cm, $|AC| = 12$ cm and $|\angle BAC| = 40°$. Find the area of the triangle, correct to one decimal place.

title: Apply the sine rule
question: In triangle $PQR$, $|\angle P| = 48°$, $|\angle Q| = 65°$ and $|QR| = 14$ cm. Find $|PR|$, correct to one decimal place.

title: Apply the cosine rule
question: In triangle $ABC$, $|AB| = 9$ cm, $|AC| = 12$ cm and $|\angle BAC| = 40^\circ$. Find $|BC|$, correct to two decimal places.

title: Solve multi-step 2D triangle problems
question: A field $ABCD$ is split by the diagonal $[AC]$. In triangle $ABC$, $|AB| = 7$ m, $|BC| = 9$ m and $|\angle ABC| = 70^\circ$. In triangle $ACD$, $|CD| = 8$ m and $|\angle ACD| = 50^\circ$. Find the area of the field, correct to one decimal place.

title: Handle the ambiguous case of the sine rule
question: In triangle $ABC$, $|BC| = 10$ cm, $|AC| = 13$ cm and $|\angle BAC| = 35^\circ$. Find the two possible values of $|\angle ABC|$, correct to one decimal place.

title: Solve 3D trigonometry problems
question: A box has a rectangular base $12$ cm by $5$ cm and a height of $6$ cm. Find the angle between a space diagonal and the base, correct to one decimal place.
